svg.text: The 18 tables of the consolidated baseline · 40 foreign keys, 16 of them the tenant's network_id · crow's-foot notation
IX (network_id, name) — the search before enrolling
UQ (network_id, cpf) — the CPF is the access identifier
the e-mail is not unique: a family shares one address
no network_id: it is a platform table, not a business one
claimed inside the write’s own transaction, never by the edge
PK (announcement_id, user_id) · read_at measures the read rate
UQ (enrollment_id, attendance_date) — attendance per DAY, never per lesson
term 1..4 · value 0..10 — the average never becomes a column
network_id did not become an arrow
Drawing 16 lines to the same target
would hide the rest of the graph,
· network — it is the tenant, it does
"it does not belong to a network".
The arrow that no longer contradicts
the code pointed the other way.
It is gone. The guardian became an
the same direction as the teacher's.
identity is a leaf in the database too:
no foreign key leaves it any more.
The crow's foot touches the child table,
the one that holds the foreign key.
Colour = module that owns the table
The line inherits the CHILD table's colour:
an arrow coloured unlike the target box
is a key that crosses modules.
What was omitted from every box
updated_at is kept by the trigger
Source: migrations/0001_initial_schema.sql. The diagram shows the schema exactly as the consolidated baseline creates it — every column, key and constraint read from that file.
Three guarantees that live half in this file and half in the code
claimPendingWriteInTransaction() runs this INSERT as the FIRST
statement of unitOfWork(): the claim and the rows it protects
commit together, and a ROLLBACK takes both. There is no
compensating DELETE anywhere in the code — the row you see
here is a write that actually happened.
Both partial indexes carry WHERE status = 'active'. One refuses
a second active row per student and year; the other serves every
read that starts from a class group's active students.
The literal has to stay a literal: parameterised, the planner
stops choosing them and the lookup turns into a scan.
One guarantee is not in this file at all: the order between closing a term and posting into it is an advisory lock on
(class_group_id, term), taken by closeTerm() and postGrades() inside their own transactions. UQ (class_group_id, term)
is what remains if that lock is ever removed.
